qualifications: The eight confirmation conversations were excluded from this policy selection, but prior project experiments have used all ten conversations. This is confirmation after prior project exposure, not globally unseen data.
Offline retrieval/context-allocation experiment from previously captured semantic top20; no reader, judge, model, native backend, provider or answer-accuracy claim.
Only the frozen candidate and control were scored. Selection reuses the existing seven-output pure selector without inspecting or scoring alternative test contexts.
Control context hashes, turn IDs, and bytes match all 1986 historical full-result questions; metrics match all 1586 confirmation questions.
The budget is a maximum of 12000 UTF-8 bytes, not an equality constraint; both policies use whole unmodified turns and the same captured top20 seeds.
The winning policy uses 236.12 more context bytes on average within the same 12,000-byte ceiling. The experiment tests its complete ordering, radius, and packing policy together.
Timing reports the existing selector that builds all seven label-free contexts plus admission overhead; it is not independent end-to-end production retrieval latency.
The policy remains an experimental benchmark context selector; this evidence does not say it is the shipped default search policy.
